mem.t: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.

lessons.title: Reconciled to God
lessons.theme: All peace begins with being reconciled to God

v: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

lessons.still: Be still and imagine yourself standing before the cross. Lay down there, one by one, your past failures and any unresolved guilt. Hear the Lord say to you, “I have reconciled you to God.” Take a deep breath and let this peace settle into the depths of your heart.
teach: If a pond's source is polluted, no amount of cleaning downstream will make the water clear. Conflict between people often stems from conflict between people and God. When we are cut off from God, there is an unspeakable unrest inside us, and that unrest turns into defensiveness, comparison and attack, eventually flowing into every relationship.

Paul says, “Being justified by faith, we have peace with God.” This peace is not a ceasefire we negotiated; it is a reconciliation God himself accomplished in Christ: “All things are of God,” who does “not reckon their trespasses to them.” The cross is the bridge of reconciliation between heaven and earth; enemies become children.

Even more wonderful, God has entrusted us with “the ministry of reconciliation.” We first receive peace, and then we can pass peace on. The mindset shift: peace does not begin with “I've sorted things out with that person,” but with “I have been reconciled to God.” Once the source is clear, the relationships downstream can become clear too.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships: first with God, then with ourselves, then with others, then with tasks. The fruit of peace is not a matter of managing our emotions by self-cultivation; once we are reconciled to God, the life of Christ flows naturally out of a self-emptied person. All things are from God, and all glory goes to God.
q: Who is God? — “All things are of God.” God took the initiative to reconcile you to himself. What kind of God does this show you?
Who am I? — Is there still some unresolved unrest between you and God?
How shall I respond? — How will you bring your reconciliation with God into one relationship today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “made peace through the blood of his cross” (Colossians 1:20). He was not a third party mediating from the middle; he took the brokenness of both sides upon himself and paid the price of reconciliation with his own body.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for reconciling me to yourself in Christ and not counting my trespasses against me. I lay all my guilt and unrest at the foot of the cross. Let your peace begin in my relationship with you and flow into my family, my workplace and my church, and make me a messenger of reconciliation. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Confess to the Lord one thing that still troubles you, and receive his forgiveness
Write “I have been reconciled to God” and put it up by your desk
For one of my 2s: share how you have experienced being reconciled to God
lessons.noon: “We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” — Lord, right now I find rest in you.

lessons.title: Peace Beyond Understanding
lessons.theme: Peace is not the absence of storms but the Lord's presence in the storm

v: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

lessons.still: Name the things that are worrying you, one at a time. With each one, open your hands as though handing it over. Finish with a word of thanks: “Lord, thank you for hearing.” Then quietly let peace stand guard at the door of your heart.
teach: Picture a painting: beside a waterfall in a raging storm, with the wind howling and spray flying, a little bird sits safely in its nest in a crevice of the rock. Peace is not the absence of the storm; it is a secure place within the storm. The peace the world offers is “the problem is solved”; the peace the Lord gives is “I am with you.”

Paul gives a concrete path: don't be anxious about anything, pray about everything, and do it with thanksgiving. The result is that God's peace will “guard” your hearts and minds. “Guard” is a military term, like soldiers garrisoning a city. Jesus said, “Not as the world gives do I give to you.” The world's peace depends on conditions; the Lord's peace depends on his presence, which is why it “surpasses all understanding”.

The fruit of peace must first grow in our own hearts before we can bring it into our relationships. An anxious heart easily infects others with anxiety; only a guarded heart can become a quiet strength in someone else's storm. The mindset shift: from “I'll have peace once I have everything under control” to “I have peace when I hand things over to God.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: Worry is often another form of the self-ruled life: I want control, I want to guarantee the outcome, which amounts to sitting on God's throne. Handing our worries to God is laying down power and returning to our place: let people be people and let God be God. Live from the heart by the Spirit, and your heart is glad; live from the head by yourself, and you are full of worry.
q: Who is God? — “My peace I give to you.” How is Jesus' peace different from the world's peace?
Who am I? — What have you been trying to control yourself, and lost your peace over?
How shall I respond? — How will you practise “prayer plus thanksgiving” to deal with worry today?
lessons.jesus: When a fierce storm arose, Jesus was asleep in the stern on a cushion. The terrified disciples woke him; he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm. The peace in his heart came before the calm on the water, and today he is in our boat too.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I hand my worries to you one by one, and I thank you for hearing me. I confess that I often want to control everything myself. Let your peace, which surpasses all understanding, guard my heart and mind, so that I can bring peace to others in their storms. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three worries, and pray through each one with thanksgiving
When you want to control the outcome today, pray silently: “Let God be God.”
For one of my 2s: when they are anxious, quietly pray with them
lessons.noon: “And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.” — Lord, right now I hand my worries to you.

lessons.title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
lessons.theme: The Lord wants me not only to enjoy peace but to make peace

v: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

lessons.still: Think of a relationship around you that is tense right now: within your family, among colleagues, in your small group. Don't rush to find a solution. First quietly bless both sides, and ask the Lord to give you the wisdom that comes from above.
teach: Some people are like matches: wherever they go, fires break out. Others are like fire extinguishers: wherever they go, things cool down. Jesus did not say “Blessed are the peace-lovers” but “Blessed are the peacemakers.” It is not just avoiding conflict and keeping ourselves clean; it is stepping into the brokenness and becoming someone who mends.

Jesus said peacemakers “shall be called children of God”, because God himself is the greatest peacemaker of all, reconciling the world to himself in Christ. James points out that the wisdom from above is “first pure, then peaceful.” True peace is not papering over the cracks or covering up right and wrong; it has purity as its foundation and mercy as its attitude.

James adds, “The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.” Here is another fruit image: peace is like a seed that must be sown and waited on before it grows into the fruit of righteousness. The mindset shift: I don't have to force both sides to reconcile immediately, but I can sow seeds of peace in every conversation.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Making peace requires the self-emptied life: not rushing to prove that we are right, not taking sides, not stirring things up. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and both sides win. Peacemakers are the very people who build God's kingdom system on earth, letting God's kingdom come between people.
q: Who is God? — God is called the God of peace. How is he doing his peacemaking work in you?
Who am I? — In conflict, are you more like a match or a fire extinguisher?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship can you sow a seed of peace today?
lessons.jesus: Among Jesus' disciples were Matthew, who had collected taxes for Rome, and Simon the Zealot, who had resisted Rome. In the world they were sworn enemies, yet beside Jesus they became brothers. Jesus is the Prince of Peace who breaks down the dividing wall of hostility.
lessons.pray: Lord of peace, make me a peacemaker, not someone who starts fires. Give me the wisdom from above that is first pure, then peaceful and full of mercy. Today, in the relationships where you have placed me, use me to sow seeds of peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Today, don't repeat a single remark that could cause misunderstanding
In a tense situation, say one thing that calms things down
For one of my 2s: if they are at odds with someone, pray with them
lessons.noon: “Blessed are the peacemakers.” — Lord, right now make me an instrument of your peace.

lessons.title: Children of Peace in the Midst of Conflict
lessons.theme: Conflict is not failure but a place where the fruit of peace can grow

v: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
“If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

lessons.still: Ask the Holy Spirit to remind you: is there someone who “has something against you”? Don't argue over who was right or wrong; just honestly admit that there is a crack in this relationship. Gently speak that person's name and place them before the Lord.
teach: When a garment gets a small hole, a few stitches will mend it if you deal with it promptly; leave it, and the tear only grows. Relationships are the same. We often think, “I'll deal with it once I've calmed down,” or “Time heals everything.” But time does not automatically mend a rift; often it only lets the wound harden into a scar.

Jesus says something startling: if you are offering your gift at the altar and remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there and go and be reconciled first. Notice: it is your brother who has something against you, not you against him. The initiative lies with me. Paul says, “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you”: I cannot control the other person's response, but I can take responsibility for my own part.

The hardest thing in conflict is letting go of “I am right.” Children of peace do not ignore right and wrong; they are willing to deal with their own part first: admitting their own faults, speaking the truth in love, and not repaying evil for evil. The mindset shift: conflict is not the end of a relationship but the building site where the Holy Spirit grows the fruit of peace.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is leaving our place and grasping power; in conflict, “I have to win” is grasping power. Humility is laying down power and returning to our place. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things: better to lose the argument than to lose a brother.
q: Who is God? — God values reconciliation even above sacrifice. What does this say about what matters to him?
Who am I? — Are you waiting for the other person to apologise first before you are willing to make peace?
How shall I respond? — For which rift will you take the first step today?
lessons.jesus: On the night he was betrayed, Peter drew his sword and cut off the ear of the high priest's servant, but Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him. In the most heated conflict, Jesus did not repay evil for evil; instead he healed a man from the enemy's side.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often wait for others to apologise first, and I often want to win in conflict. Give me the courage to go and be reconciled first, and to do all I can to live at peace with everyone. In conflict, help me let go of “I am right” and let you reign. Heal the rifts between me and others. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: take the initiative and send a message of reconciliation about a rift
In a disagreement today, say first, “I was in the wrong too”
Write down your most common reaction in conflict, and hand it to the Lord
lessons.noon: “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.” — Lord, right now I am willing to take the first step toward peace.

lessons.title: Making Peace with My 2
lessons.theme: Let the peace of Christ rule in your heart and work in your relationships

v: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,

lessons.still: Open your “My 2 List” and ask the Holy Spirit to show you which relationship most needs peace. Quietly bless that person, and ask the Lord to show you one small thing you can do for this relationship this week.
teach: In a ball game, when the referee blows the whistle, play stops and every player has to listen. Paul says, “Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts,” and the word for “rule” originally carried the sense of acting as umpire. When I am with my 2, I must let the peace of Christ blow the whistle in my heart, rather than letting anger, hurt feelings or pride make the call.

Hebrews says, “Pursue peace with all people, and holiness,” setting peace and holiness side by side. “Pursue” is an active word, like a hunter chasing his quarry. Peace does not arrive by itself; we have to pursue it actively. And true peace is bound up with holiness: it does not compromise the truth but receives one another within the truth.

This week we have walked through being reconciled to God, peace in our hearts, making peace, and reconciliation in the midst of conflict. Now we are to make peace concretely with one of our 2s. But peace often takes time; people don't change overnight. Next week we will learn a fruit closely tied to peace: patience.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God's kingdom system is fulfilling the Lord's Prayer: your kingdom come, your will be done on earth. Peace at home, at work and in the church is what the kingdom of heaven looks like on earth. Peace is not a matter of cultivating a better temper by our own effort; it is letting the peace of Christ rule in a self-emptied heart.
q: Who is God? — The peace of Christ is willing to “umpire” in your heart. What comfort does this bring you?
Who am I? — When you face your 2, who usually blows the whistle in your heart: peace, anger or pride?
How shall I respond? — This week, what one thing will you do to make peace with which 2?
lessons.jesus: When the risen Jesus first appeared to his disciples, his very first words were, “Peace be to you!” These were the disciples who had scattered and fled when he needed them most, yet he spoke not one word of reproach. He gave them peace first and restored the broken relationship.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, let your peace rule in my heart. When anger and hurt want to make the call, blow the whistle of peace. This week I want to make peace with one of my 2s; give me wisdom and courage, and a thankful heart. May your kingdom come in our relationships. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: take one concrete peacemaking action this week
When you feel anger rising today, pray silently: “Let the peace of Christ rule.”
Before bed, pray with a thankful heart for each of today's relationships
lessons.noon: “And let the peace of God rule in your hearts” — Lord, right now blow the whistle of peace in my heart.
